</dependency>

diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The organizer hint points to defects in the Maven build workflow guidance: it underspecifies/incorrectly specifies toolchain selection and the contract for reproducing failures and build commands, and it lacks/has incorrect guidance for dependency resolution and safe modification scope in nested test (Invoker/IT) projects. These issues are localized to the maven-build-lifecycle skill document; other Maven dependency/plugin skills are generic and not implicated by the hint.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The document’s build reproduction section is incomplete (only a cd command) and the 'Build-repair artifact contract' numbering is inconsistent (starts at 2). Per hint, guidance around selecting the correct build toolchain (e.g., Maven wrapper vs system Maven, Java version) and the conventions for failure reproduction/build commands is unclear or missing. Additionally, it lacks clear instructions for handling nested test projects (e.g., maven-invoker-plugin integration test projects under src/it or similar): how their dependencies are resolved (local repo vs reactor) and what files are in-scope to change vs not (templates, expected outputs, injected POMs). This can mislead repairs or cause changes to be applied in the wrong place, breaking evaluation expectations.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Edit maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md to (1) fix the artifact contract numbering and explicitly restate required paths (failed_reasons.txt, patch_1.diff) while preserving existing intent; (2) add a concise, authoritative 'toolchain selection' subsection: prefer ./mvnw when present, otherwise mvn; record Maven/Java versions; mention checking JAVA_HOME and using the project’s required JDK; (3) add a 'minimal failure reproduction' command convention: run mvn -e -X only when needed, start with mvn -q? no; specify typical commands (mvn -V -e test, mvn -pl … -am test) and capturing logs; (4) add a dedicated section on nested test/Invoker projects: explain that src/it projects often use their own pom.xml copied at test time, may rely on the built artifacts from the reactor or local repo, and that fixes should generally be in the main modules’ POMs/source or in the IT template inputs when the test itself is wrong; clarify modification scope: avoid editing generated/target directories, prefer editing src/it/**/pom.xml templates or invoker settings only when the failure originates there; (5) provide a short checklist to determine whether dependency changes should be made in parent/module POM vs IT POM template, and how to force installation to local repo when invoker needs it (e.g., mvn -DskipTests install before ITs).
